{"path":"effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_anthropic-claude-haiku-5-5_01.html","edit_description":"Create a complete, self-contained HTML5 file (inline CSS and JavaScript only, no external libraries, no WebGL; Canvas 2D only) implementing a realtime Gouraud-shaded rotating cube. Requirements, precisely:

PAGE: black body, margin 0, full-window <canvas id="c"> sized to window.innerWidth/innerHeight (handle window resize). A small HUD div (top-left, monospace, light text) shows "FPS: NN" updated once per second, plus a help line "W: wireframe   P: pause". No alerts.

GEOMETRY: cube with vertices at (±1,±1,±1) scaled by 1. Six faces, each split into 2 triangles (12 triangles total, 36 indices). Each face gets a distinct base color (e.g. RGB arrays). Each cube corner (vertex) gets a smooth normal = normalize(corner position) so that Gouraud interpolation shows a visible gradient across faces. Store per-triangle: 3 vertex indices and face base color.

MATH: write small helpers: mat3 multiply, rotX(a), rotY(b), rotZ(c) producing 3x3 row-major matrices; mulVec(m, v); normalize; dot; cross. Each frame: angles ax, ay, az advance with delta time (paused = no advance). Rotate each vertex and each vertex normal by the combined matrix R = Rz*Ry*Rx.

LIGHTING (per-vertex Lambert): a point light orbits the cube on a circle/ellipse in world space (e.g. radius 3.0, y oscillating), with position L(t) computed from time t (which only advances when not paused). For each vertex compute the world-space position P and normal N (after rotation); lightDir = normalize(L - P); diffuse = max(0, dot(N, lightDir)); intensity = ambient 0.15 + 0.85*diffuse. Vertex color = faceBaseColor * intensity (per channel, clamp 0..255). Store the lit color per vertex; these are the values interpolated during rasterization.

PROJECTION: camera at z distance 6 looking down -z in view space: view point = (x, y, z + 6) after rotation (cube center at origin). Perspective: sx = cx + x * f / vz, sy = cy - y * f / vz, where f = 0.8*min(width,height)/2 * something sensible (e.g. f = min(w,h)*0.9*(6/ (2*... )) — choose so the cube fills roughly 40-50% of the smaller screen dimension). Keep vz for depth.

BACKFACE CULLING: for each triangle compute face normal in view space from the rotated vertices (cross of edges) and test against view direction: visible if dot(faceNormal, -viewPos_of_first_vertex) > 0 (i.e. facing toward camera). Skip invisible triangles in both shaded and wireframe modes.

RASTERIZATION (Gouraud): for each visible triangle, compute projected screen coordinates and lit colors for its 3 vertices. Rasterize into a single ImageData buffer (use a Uint32Array view over imageData.data for speed, little-endian packing: 0xFF000000 | b<<16 | g<<8 | r) with a Float32Array z-buffer of inverse depth (1/vz) per pixel, cleared each frame to 0, so overlapping triangles resolve correctly (use depth test: larger 1/vz wins). For each triangle: bounding box clipped to canvas; compute edge functions / barycentric weights (w0,w1,w2) per pixel center; if all >= 0 (handle both winding orders by computing area sign and normalizing), interpolate color channels r,g,b linearly with barycentric weights (Gouraud) and interpolate 1/vz linearly for depth; perform z-test and write pixel. Fill background with dark color (e.g. 0x101018) each frame. After rasterizing all triangles, ctx.putImageData(imageData, 0, 0).

WIREFRAME (toggle with key W, case-insensitive): when wireframe is on, do NOT fill triangles; instead, after clearing background, draw the visible triangle edges with ctx.strokeStyle light color (e.g. rgba(0,255,200,0.9)), lineWidth 1, using ctx.beginPath/moveTo/lineTo/closePath/stroke per frame. Shaded mode is the default. Canvas must be redrawn each frame in either mode.

MOVING LIGHT INDICATOR: project the light position L (using the same projection, view transform not applied to light beyond the camera offset: treat light in view space as (Lx, Ly, Lz + 6) without cube rotation) and draw a small yellow filled circle (radius ~6px) with a soft glow (ctx.shadowBlur) on top of the canvas, after putImageData. Only drawn when projected depth > 0.

CONTROLS: keydown listener: 'w'/'W' toggles wireframe, 'p'/'P' toggles pause. Paused state freezes cube rotation and the light's orbit motion but rendering still continues (so the frame stays visible). Show "PAUSED" text on the canvas when paused (top-center).

LOOP: requestAnimationFrame loop with delta time clamped to 0.05s. FPS counter: count frames, every 1000 ms set HUD text to "FPS: " + count, reset count. Use performance.now().

CODE STYLE: JavaScript camelCase for functions and variables, clean comments, single file, valid HTML5 with <!DOCTYPE html>, <meta charset="utf-8">, <title>Gouraud Shaded Cube</title>. Must run directly in a browser with no build step and no console errors. Keep the code readable and well-structured (sections: math, geometry, lighting, projection, rasterizer, UI loop)."}
